metadata.title: Branching Pattern Modeling: A Geometric Measure Theory Approach
metadata.abstract: This article is based on a lecture given at Westlake University. It aims to introduce students to an application of geometric measure theory in modeling branched patterns found in both living and nonliving systems. We begin with the Eulerian framework of ramified optimal transportation, including discrete transport paths, their basic properties, numerical approximation, and the passage to general transport paths represented by rectifiable currents. We then describe an application to the dynamic formation of a plant leaf, where branching venation patterns arise from a balance between metabolic benefit and transportation cost. Finally, we review landscape functions associated with transport paths and explain how two existing approaches can be unified within a broader family of rectifiable $1$-currents. We conclude by indicating several open directions related to Gilbert-type network problems, biological modeling, and numerical approximation.

analysis.progressType: 分支最优输运与叶脉模型讲义
analysis.workSummary: 从 Eulerian 分支输运的离散路径与数值近似出发，过渡到以可求长流表示的一般输运路径，再介绍植物叶脉由代谢收益与运输成本平衡形成的模型。
analysis.breakthrough: 在更广的可求长 1-流框架下比较并统一两种既有景观函数处理方式，梳理 Gilbert 型网络与数值近似中的开放问题。
analysis.limitations: 本文由讲座发展而来，主要是概念与模型综述。摘要未给普遍的数值误差界或植物模型验证结果。 当前数学解读依据摘要，尚未逐步审读证明。

aiReview.note: 对该版本全部可提取页面做 AI 披露关键词检索，并核对命中段落；这不是对整篇数学证明的审读。完整30页文本、原候选和点写AI、拆行模型名等补检未见作者使用生成式AI声明。文中的数值近似与运输网络建模属于研究主题。判断限于该版本未观察到披露。

analysis.priorityReason: 适合作为几何测度论和分支输运的入门材料。
